title: 5 Best ClickHouse Frontend Builders in 2026
summary: ClickHouse is fast enough to power interactive apps. Five ways to build a frontend on it, and where each one stops.
body_markdown:
ClickHouse answers analytical queries over billions of rows in well under a second, which makes it fast enough to sit behind interactive screens, not just nightly reports. A ClickHouse frontend can be a dashboard, a customer-facing usage page or an internal tool where support looks up a user's recent events. Which tool fits depends on whether people only read charts or also need to act on what they see.


Below are five ClickHouse frontend builders, with the point where each one stops. For SQL clients, see the[best ClickHouse GUI clients](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-clickhouse-gui-clients/) .


## The five options at a glance


Option Builds Can write data? Cost


Jet Admin Internal tools, portals and dashboards Yes Free plan; paid tiers


Grafana Real-time dashboards No Free open source; paid cloud


Apache Superset BI dashboards and exploration No Free, open source


Metabase BI dashboards and questions Limited Free open source; paid plans


Retool Developer-built internal tools Yes Free tier; paid per user


## The options


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to ClickHouse and builds a frontend that combines analytics with action: a support screen showing a customer's recent events next to their account record from Postgres, with buttons to issue a credit or open a ticket. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or in code. Every screen runs bounded queries you designed, so nobody triggers an accidental full scan.


Roles decide who sees which data, and people sign in to the app rather than getting ClickHouse credentials. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it is not an ad hoc exploration tool; analysts will prefer Superset or a SQL client.


### 2. Grafana


Grafana's ClickHouse data source makes it a popular choice for real-time operational dashboards and observability on ClickHouse.


**Where it stops:** dashboards are read-only, and business users often find Grafana's interface technical.


### 3. Apache Superset


Superset connects to ClickHouse for SQL exploration and dashboards, and is free and open source.


**Where it stops:** it is for analysis, not workflows or record editing, and running it yourself takes effort.


### 4. Metabase


Metabase supports ClickHouse through its driver and offers an approachable question builder and dashboards.


**Where it stops:** it is BI-first; operational screens with forms and approvals are outside its scope.


### 5. Retool


Retool connects to ClickHouse, and developers build internal tools with charts, tables and actions.


**Where it stops:** per-user pricing and developer maintenance.


## Which to use


- **Teams need to see ClickHouse data and act on it:** Jet Admin.
- **You need real-time operational dashboards:** Grafana.
- **Analysts need exploration and BI:** Superset or Metabase.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool.


## Start with what people do next


If people only look at charts, a BI tool is enough. If they need to act on what they see,[connect ClickHouse to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/clickhouse) and build the screens around that action.
